lessons.title: What installation qualification establishes
lessons.objective: Distinguish installed configuration from operating performance.

scenes.title: From design to installation
scenes.narration: Welcome to Module Four, Installation Qualification, or I Q. We continue with the fictional V-201 oral-liquid mixing vessel. The design review described what was intended. Now the team compares the installed system with the accepted design and manufacturer recommendations. Every identifier and observation in this module is invented for training. No real equipment has been qualified.
scenes.description: From design to installation: the evidence map groups DESIGN, INSTALLED, COMPARE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Three different evidence questions
scenes.narration: A drawing shows a temperature sensor connection. A walkdown identifies which sensor is installed at that connection. An operational challenge examines how the assembled loop behaves. These answer different questions. Finding the correct tag does not demonstrate alarm response, and a successful alarm test does not repair missing material identification. Keep each conclusion tied to the evidence actually obtained.
scenes.description: Three different evidence questions: the evidence map groups DRAWING, WALKDOWN, CHALLENGE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Set the system boundary
scenes.narration: For our case, the installation boundary includes the vessel, agitator, outlet components, instruments and defined utility connections. The upstream utility plant has its own qualification scope. Record where one system ends and another begins. A qualified water system does not automatically prove that a new branch has the correct connection or that its delivered water is suitable.
scenes.description: Set the system boundary: the evidence map groups UPSTREAM, INTERFACE, VESSEL. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Limit the conclusion
scenes.narration: The teaching conclusion is limited to installation evidence reviewed against the defined baseline. It is not permission to manufacture a batch. Operational and performance verification remain separate needs. Where stages are combined in an approved approach, the underlying evidence questions still remain visible. Your first activity separates installation observations from claims that require later studies.
scenes.description: Limit the conclusion: the evidence map groups OBSERVED, UNRESOLVED, RECOMMEND. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Classify: sensor serial matches schedule; alarm stops heating; batch blend is uniform. Explain the evidence boundary.
lessons.model: The first is installation identity evidence. Alarm response needs a defined operational challenge. Blend uniformity needs a justified performance/process study; neither is proven by identity alone.

quiz.question: Which finding is directly an installation identity check?
options: Alarm response under simulated sensor failure
Sensor serial matches the controlled instrument schedule
Blend uniformity across the batch
quiz.feedback: The serial comparison addresses installed identity; the other choices require functional or performance evidence.

lessons.title: Prepare the IQ baseline and protocol
lessons.objective: Define what will be checked, how, and against which controlled criteria.

scenes.title: Reconcile the input package
scenes.narration: The fictional installation package contains the user requirements, design-review outcome, accepted drawings and an installation protocol. List identifiers and revisions before the walkdown. An email attachment labelled final is not enough to establish its approval status. If the valve drawing changed after design review, identify the change and its accepted impact before relying on the old conclusion.
scenes.description: Reconcile the input package: the evidence map groups URS / DQ, DRAWINGS, PROTOCOL. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Write an executable check
scenes.narration: Replace verify installation is satisfactory with a check another trained person can repeat. For example, compare the installed outlet valve tag and model against schedule revision C, using a safe visual inspection and the identified manufacturer plate. Define what information will be recorded and how inaccessible markings will be handled. Do not leave the acceptance rule to be invented after seeing the result.
scenes.description: Write an executable check: the evidence map groups REQUIREMENT, METHOD, RECORD. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Check readiness safely
scenes.narration: Before inspecting, confirm training, access arrangements and any required isolation with the responsible engineering team. Do not remove guards, open electrical panels or disconnect a process line merely to complete a checklist. If a marking cannot be reached safely, record that limitation and arrange an approved method. Schedule pressure does not turn an unsafe inspection into acceptable evidence.
scenes.description: Check readiness safely: the evidence map groups TRAINING, SAFE ACCESS, TOOLS. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Resolve a missing criterion
scenes.narration: Suppose the drawing shows a clearance but provides no approved minimum. Measuring a convenient distance and then calling it acceptable creates a circular argument. Raise the missing requirement to the responsible design and quality functions. The team may collect a clearly identified observation, but acceptance of that feature remains unresolved until the criterion and approach are properly established.
scenes.description: Resolve a missing criterion: the evidence map groups MEASURED, NO CRITERION, UNRESOLVED. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Write an IQ check for outlet valve identity with baseline, criterion, safe method and evidence fields.
lessons.model: Name the controlled schedule and revision, required tag/model, visual method, actual observed identifiers, evidence reference, executor/date and discrepancy route. Confirm safe access; do not infer acceptance from an unapproved drawing.
worked: VAL-V201 revision C, fictional accepted schedule

quiz.question: The protocol has no criterion for a clearance measurement. What is defensible?
options: Resolve the missing criterion before deciding acceptance
Use the measured clearance as the acceptance limit
Accept it because the supplier installed it
quiz.feedback: A result cannot define its own acceptance criterion.

lessons.title: Conduct a physical installation walkdown
lessons.objective: Match the actual arrangement to controlled installation evidence.

scenes.title: Start at the equipment plate
scenes.narration: The walkdown starts with equipment identity, not a copied supplier checklist. Compare the vessel tag, manufacturer model, serial number and location with the controlled package. A matching tag attached to a different vessel would not establish identity. Record discrepancies individually so a later reviewer can tell which identifiers matched and which remained uncertain.
scenes.description: Start at the equipment plate: the evidence map groups TAG, MODEL / SERIAL, LOCATION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Trace components in place
scenes.narration: Work through the installed arrangement systematically. Identify the agitator assembly and supports, then trace the outlet and instrument connections against the relevant drawing. Confirm required orientation and accessible features using the approved method. Do not run the agitator to infer installation conformity when the authorized activity is a static inspection. Functional rotation checks belong in the defined test plan.
scenes.description: Trace components in place: the evidence map groups AGITATOR, OUTLET, SENSOR. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Inspect the removal envelope
scenes.narration: The design allowed a rear instrument to slide out for maintenance, but the installed pipe rack crosses that removal envelope. A front-facing photograph misses this problem. Compare the full maintenance envelope with the approved arrangement and manufacturer requirements. No universal clearance is supplied here. Document the obstruction and its consequences without inventing a numerical GMP minimum.
scenes.description: Plan view: the dashed instrument-removal path intersects the adjacent pipe rack; no minimum clearance is implied.

scenes.title: Record what was inaccessible
scenes.narration: A covered connection cannot be recorded as verified solely because its neighbour matches. Record the inaccessible item, why it could not be examined and the agreed follow-up. If suitable controlled evidence supports another verification method, justify its applicability. Distinguish direct observation from document review so the evidence does not appear stronger than it is.
scenes.description: Record what was inaccessible: the evidence map groups INACCESSIBLE, NOT CHECKED, FOLLOW-UP. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Write a finding for a rear instrument blocked by a pipe rack. Separate observation, criterion and impact.
lessons.model: Record the location and obstruction, cite the approved removal envelope/manufacturer instruction, identify maintenance implications, assign an action and specify reinspection. Do not invent a clearance value.
worked: Pipe rack crosses rear instrument removal path
Instrument cannot be removed as intended

quiz.question: An inaccessible connection is next to one that matches the drawing. What is its status?
options: Accepted by similarity with the visible connection
Accepted because the supplier signed the drawing
Not yet verified unless an applicable alternative is justified
quiz.feedback: Each conclusion needs applicable evidence; adjacency is not verification.

lessons.title: Verify materials and component traceability
lessons.objective: Link the installed contact path to applicable material evidence.

scenes.title: Map the contact components
scenes.narration: Follow the product-contact path through the fictional vessel. Include the agitator, gaskets, valve seats and transfer connection, not only the metal shell. The installation check asks whether the specified materials are actually represented by the installed components and their evidence. A certificate for the vessel body does not identify an elastomer fitted later.
scenes.description: Map the contact components: the evidence map groups BODY, GASKET, OUTLET. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Connect item to certificate
scenes.narration: A certificate says material grade X, but which installed item does it describe? Use the applicable identifiers and controlled supplier traceability to link the record to the component. The precise method depends on the component and project. Do not require one universal certificate format or assume every gasket has a readable individual serial number. Evaluate the traceability actually available.
scenes.description: Connect item to certificate: the evidence map groups COMPONENT, LOT / ID, CERTIFICATE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Treat missing links as gaps
scenes.narration: In our example, the vessel certificate is available but the installed gasket lot cannot be linked to its material record. Keep the gasket finding open. The vessel certificate does not fill that gap. Obtain applicable traceability, or use an authorized corrective approach followed by verification. Changing a label without evidence would only conceal the uncertainty.
scenes.description: Treat missing links as gaps: the evidence map groups BODY: LINKED, GASKET: GAP, EVIDENCE NEEDED. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Keep suitability and identity separate
scenes.narration: Material identity and material suitability are related but different questions. The design review should have considered intended exposure, while installation evidence identifies what was fitted. If an authorized substitution changes the material, assess the compatibility and qualification implications through change control. Do not declare cleaning effectiveness solely because the installed material matches a certificate.
scenes.description: Keep suitability and identity separate: the evidence map groups SPECIFIED, FITTED, SUITABILITY. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Build a three-row contact-material register and describe how to handle a missing gasket traceability link.
lessons.model: Include body, gasket and outlet component; record specification, installed identifier, evidence reference and status. Keep the gasket unresolved, obtain applicable evidence or authorized correction, and reassess any material change.
worked: Part identifier linked to accepted specification

quiz.question: The body certificate is available but gasket identity is unresolved. What follows?
options: Accept both because they share the product path
Keep the gasket gap open and obtain applicable evidence
Use the body grade as the gasket material
quiz.feedback: Certificate scope does not extend automatically to other contact components.

lessons.title: Verify piping and utility interfaces
lessons.objective: Check the installed connection while preserving upstream qualification boundaries.

scenes.title: Trace source to point of use
scenes.narration: Trace the installed branch from its defined source to the vessel connection against the controlled piping diagram. Check the specified route, isolation and identifiers using safe methods. Do not assume a pipe has the intended contents because its colour looks familiar. A label and the actual connection must agree with the system information.
scenes.description: Trace source to point of use: the evidence map groups SOURCE, ISOLATION, CONNECTION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Read labels and direction
scenes.narration: For fixed pipework, contents identification and applicable flow direction help prevent mistakes. Compare labels with the route and controlled drawing, including places where lines cross. A correct label on the wrong connected branch remains a discrepancy. Record the location so the engineering team can resolve the actual connection rather than merely replacing the label.
scenes.description: Read labels and direction: the evidence map groups CONTENTS, DIRECTION, ACTUAL ROUTE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Separate connection from quality
scenes.narration: The branch may be installed as drawn while the required utility-quality evidence is still unavailable. Record those as separate statuses. A pressure indication alone cannot establish chemical or microbiological suitability. Determine what qualification and sampling evidence applies to the intended use through the approved project approach, rather than borrowing limits from an unrelated sterile process.
scenes.description: Separate connection from quality: the evidence map groups CONNECTED, QUALITY DATA, READINESS. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Assess a changed branch
scenes.narration: A late branch addition may affect the upstream system as well as the receiving vessel. Identify the changed configuration and assess the required installation and other verification before use. Do not assume that the original utility qualification covers every future extension. Our workbook asks which records and responsible system owners must be linked before closing the interface.
scenes.description: Assess a changed branch: the evidence map groups OLD SYSTEM, NEW BRANCH, IMPACT REVIEW. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: List separate evidence for a correctly installed utility connection and suitable delivered utility quality.
lessons.model: Installation evidence includes route, isolation, labels and drawing comparison. Quality evidence follows the approved utility qualification and relevant point-of-use requirements. Cross-reference both; neither substitutes for the other.

quiz.question: The pressure gauge reads normally. What is still unresolved?
options: Chemical and microbiological suitability of the utility
Whether the gauge has any readable indication
Whether the observation can be recorded
quiz.feedback: A pressure reading does not establish utility quality.

lessons.title: Review instruments and calibration evidence
lessons.objective: Check identity, range, calibration relevance and the effect of discrepancies.

scenes.title: Identify the installed chain
scenes.narration: Trace the installed measurement chain from sensing element to displayed value. Record the relevant identifiers, locations, ranges and configuration against the approved schedule. A display tag does not prove which sensor feeds it. Installation evidence provides the configuration baseline for later assembled-loop checks; it does not by itself establish accuracy throughout operation.
scenes.description: Identify the installed chain: the evidence map groups SENSOR, TRANSMITTER, DISPLAY. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Read beyond the sticker
scenes.narration: A calibration sticker is a starting point for locating the record. Review whether the certificate identifies the correct instrument and whether its range, points, method, results and status support the intended check. Consider uncertainty and the applicable decision rule where relevant. A current date on an unrelated instrument certificate cannot justify using the installed device.
scenes.description: Read beyond the sticker: the evidence map groups IDENTITY, COVERAGE, RESULTS. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Compare the observed error
scenes.narration: For this fictional arithmetic exercise, the reference is forty point zero degrees Celsius and the indication is forty point four. Indication minus reference gives plus zero point four degrees. With a teaching limit of plus or minus zero point five, the magnitude is within that simple limit. This is not a full calibration acceptance decision; uncertainty, method and the approved decision rule still matter.
scenes.description: The calculation panel compares 40.0 °C reference with 40.4 °C indication; the displayed +0.4 °C is signed error, not uncertainty.

scenes.title: Handle an unsuitable instrument
scenes.narration: If an instrument is outside its required calibration status, identify which checks relied on it and assess their validity. Do not simply obtain a new certificate and assume earlier readings remain valid. The investigation may require additional evidence or repeated checks under an approved approach. Record the basis for the decision and retain the original observations.
scenes.description: Handle an unsuitable instrument: the evidence map groups STATUS GAP, AFFECTED DATA, FOLLOW-UP. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Calculate indication error for 40.4 °C versus 40.0 °C, then identify information needed beyond the arithmetic.
lessons.model: Error is +0.4 °C, within the fictional ±0.5 °C magnitude limit. Confirm instrument identity, applicable method/range, uncertainty, decision rule and calibration status before concluding suitability.

quiz.question: A calibration certificate belongs to a different serial number. What is defensible?
options: Accept it if the due date is current
Accept it if both instruments have the same range
Resolve identity before relying on that certificate
quiz.feedback: Matching range and dates do not establish certificate applicability.

lessons.title: Assemble supplier and configuration records
lessons.objective: Make the installed baseline maintainable without confusing documentation with functional validation.

scenes.title: Collect usable instructions
scenes.narration: Collect the supplier instructions and maintenance requirements applicable to the installed model and revision. A large folder is not necessarily a usable handover. Check that the team can identify the correct document and that referenced drawings or schedules are available. Superseded manuals should not silently become the basis for maintaining the installed configuration.
scenes.description: Collect usable instructions: the evidence map groups INSTALLED MODEL, APPLICABLE MANUAL, MAINTENANCE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Record control configuration
scenes.narration: For the vessel control system, identify the relevant hardware, software version and configuration baseline through the approved approach. A version screenshot can support identification, but it does not establish that permissions, audit trails, alarms or backup restoration work adequately. Plan the applicable computerised-system validation separately; this introductory installation module does not claim complete Annex Eleven compliance.
scenes.description: Record control configuration: the evidence map groups HARDWARE, VERSION, CONFIGURATION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Connect maintenance readiness
scenes.narration: Link the supplier maintenance requirements to responsible site functions and the resources needed for the next authorized activity. For our case, a rear instrument requires a specific removal tool and accessible space. Record missing resources and their implications. Do not describe a task as established merely because a supplier manual mentions it.
scenes.description: Connect maintenance readiness: the evidence map groups TASK, OWNER, RESOURCES. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Review supplier test reuse
scenes.narration: A supplier test may be useful when its method, data and configuration are applicable and its reuse is justified. Consider what transport and installation could have changed. A factory photograph cannot prove that a field connection was installed correctly after shipment. Retain the rationale for what is reused and the site verification still required.
scenes.description: Review supplier test reuse: the evidence map groups FACTORY DATA, IMPACT REVIEW, SITE EVIDENCE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Prepare a handover index for instructions, configuration and supplier evidence, including one limitation.
lessons.model: Index document identifier, revision, installed-model applicability, location and owner. Explain that a software-version record establishes identity only; define separate functional validation. Justify any supplier evidence reuse.

quiz.question: A software-version screenshot is attached. What does it support by itself?
options: Identification of the observed software version
Adequacy of all access and audit-trail controls
Successful backup restoration under failure
quiz.feedback: Version identity is not functional validation.

lessons.title: Execute and record defensible observations
lessons.objective: Preserve the relationship between criteria, observations and original evidence.

scenes.title: Capture the actual result
scenes.narration: An installation record should make the comparison understandable. For the valve identity check, record the actual model and tag, the referenced schedule and the outcome. A tick without the required observation may leave a reviewer unable to reconstruct the decision. Use the approved form and record the work when performed, not from memory at the end of the week.
scenes.description: Capture the actual result: the evidence map groups CRITERION, OBSERVATION, ATTRIBUTION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Use photographs with context
scenes.narration: A photograph can support an observation if the relevant feature is readable and its relationship to the check is clear. Record location, subject and the controlled evidence reference. A cropped image of a plate without the equipment context may be ambiguous. Photographs supplement the specified verification method; they are not automatically sufficient for every installation characteristic.
scenes.description: Use photographs with context: the evidence map groups SUBJECT, LOCATION, CHECK REFERENCE. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Correct without obscuring
scenes.narration: Suppose a handwritten serial number contains a transposed digit. Correct it using the approved documentation procedure, preserving the original entry and recording the required attribution and date, with a reason where appropriate. Do not erase the original or backdate the correction. For electronic records, use the controlled system process rather than an untracked replacement file.
scenes.description: Correct without obscuring: the evidence map groups ORIGINAL, CORRECTION, ATTRIBUTION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Explain incomplete fields
scenes.narration: Not applicable, not checked and failed are different statuses. A check outside the approved system scope needs a justified not-applicable basis. An inaccessible feature is not checked. A verified mismatch is a discrepancy. Keeping these statuses distinct prevents a completed-looking form from implying that evidence exists where it does not.
scenes.description: Explain incomplete fields: the evidence map groups NOT APPLICABLE, NOT CHECKED, MISMATCH. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Rewrite “all items OK” as an evidence-linked valve check, then explain an uninspected hidden connection.
lessons.model: Record actual tag/model, location, comparator revision and evidence reference with execution details. Mark the hidden connection not checked with reason and follow-up; do not call it not applicable just to complete the form.

quiz.question: A hidden connection could not be inspected. Which entry is accurate?
options: Not applicable because access was difficult
Not checked, with reason and follow-up
Passed because no defect was visible
quiz.feedback: Lack of access does not demonstrate conformity or justify a scope exclusion.

lessons.title: Investigate discrepancies and manage changes
lessons.objective: Keep failed checks, corrective work and re-verification traceable.

scenes.title: Describe the mismatch
scenes.narration: The accepted schedule specifies valve model A, while the installed plate shows model B. Record the mismatch and its exact location. Do not decide from the model number alone whether the difference is harmless. Assess relevant materials, connection, cleaning and functional implications with the responsible experts. Retain the original observation even if the supplier later replaces the valve.
scenes.description: Describe the mismatch: the evidence map groups REQUIRED: A, OBSERVED: B, IMPACT UNKNOWN. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Choose a controlled action
scenes.narration: Correction may restore the specified valve, or a proposed design change may require an authorized assessment. These are not the same route. Do not revise the acceptance criterion merely to match what arrived. Define what verification follows the approved action and whether earlier checks or later tests are affected. Keep the decision and supporting rationale linked to the finding.
scenes.description: Choose a controlled action: the evidence map groups INVESTIGATE, AUTHORIZE ACTION, VERIFY. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Verify closure evidence
scenes.narration: A purchase order for the replacement is not closure evidence. After the authorized action, obtain the specified installation evidence and assess any related implications. Retain the original failure and the subsequent result as separate records. A clean second result should not erase the history or imply that the first configuration had always complied.
scenes.description: Verify closure evidence: the evidence map groups ORDERED ≠ CLOSED, REINSPECT, REVIEW. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Limit conditional progression
scenes.narration: Conditional progression is specific to the next qualification activity and requires a documented no-significant-impact assessment and responsible authorization. For example, an unresolved gasket issue may prevent wetted-system challenges even if a separately assessed dry control-display check could proceed. This is an illustration, not permission. Do not use a high completion percentage as a substitute for the assessment.
scenes.description: Limit conditional progression: the evidence map groups OPEN FINDING, DEFINED ACTIVITY, AUTHORIZATION. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Draft a discrepancy entry for the wrong valve and identify what is required before closure or limited progression.
lessons.model: Record expected/actual model and evidence, assess impact, use the controlled correction/change route, define reinspection and retain history. Any limited OQ progression needs an activity-specific no-significant-impact assessment and authorization.

quiz.question: The replacement valve has been ordered. Is the installation finding closed?
options: Yes, because purchasing accepted the action
Yes, because the supplier promised the correct model
No, applicable correction and verification evidence are still needed
quiz.feedback: An order is a planned action, not evidence of installed correction.

lessons.title: Report IQ and hand over to OQ
lessons.objective: Summarize evidence, limitations and authorized next steps without overstating readiness.

scenes.title: Reconcile the evidence index
scenes.narration: Before reporting, reconcile the executed checks with the evidence index and finding register. Missing attachments, ambiguous revisions and unexplained blanks can change the interpretation of a result. In our fictional package, the team confirms which checks are supported and which remain unresolved. This review does not create evidence; it tests whether the existing record supports the proposed conclusion.
scenes.description: Reconcile the evidence index: the evidence map groups CHECKS, ATTACHMENTS, REPORT. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Do not average away a gap
scenes.narration: Nine of ten checks have supporting evidence, giving ninety percent numerical coverage. The remaining item is the unresolved gasket-material link. A high percentage does not make that gap acceptable. Evaluate its significance and the proposed next activity. The course practice score and this coverage calculation are learning aids, not regulatory release thresholds.
scenes.description: Nine supported cells and one unresolved cell illustrate 90% coverage; the unresolved material gap remains decision-relevant.

scenes.title: Write a bounded recommendation
scenes.narration: The recommendation should identify the installed scope reviewed, the evidence baseline, deviations and any restrictions. State the specific next-stage activity recommended for authorization rather than ready for production. Transfer the configuration records and unresolved dependencies to the operational-qualification team so their tests use the right system and do not assume a finding has disappeared.
scenes.description: Write a bounded recommendation: the evidence map groups SCOPE, RESTRICTIONS, OQ HANDOVER. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

scenes.title: Defend the handover
scenes.narration: For the capstone, trace one conclusion back to its criterion, observation and evidence. Explain the remaining gasket finding and identify which proposed activities depend on it. Then draft a recommendation for the responsible reviewers. This self-study exercise is not independent competence certification, an executed qualification package or a substitute for site procedures and qualified human review.
scenes.description: Defend the handover: the evidence map groups TRACE EVIDENCE, EXPLAIN GAP, RECOMMEND. These three related review topics correspond to the narrated explanation; the map is not a physical equipment drawing.

lessons.activity: Prepare a short IQ handover with scope, evidence references, open gasket finding, restrictions and proposed OQ decision.
lessons.model: State the baseline and supported installation checks, retain the gasket gap, hold dependent wetted tests and request a documented decision for any separate activity. Include owners and evidence locations; 90% coverage does not authorize progression.
worked: Responsible review of defined OQ readiness

quiz.question: Nine checks are supported and one important material gap remains. What governs progression?
options: The significance of the gap and authorized next activity
The fact that coverage exceeds the course practice score
The number of pages already signed
quiz.feedback: Coverage does not replace impact assessment and authorization.
